alt: Handwritten notes on the Porter stemming algorithm: stemming is a simplified form of morphological analysis used to find the root word; the Porter stemmer is a simple rule-based algorithm with 5 sets of rules, known for its speed and simplicity. A consonant is a letter other than a, e, i, o, u and y preceded by a consonant.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten notes giving the form of every word as [C][VC]^m[V]: C is a string of one or more consonants, V a string of one or more vowels and m is the measure of the word or word part. The vowel line in these notes says y preceded by vowels; the correct rule is y preceded by a consonant.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten worked examples of the measure. TREE is consonants CC then vowels VV, so m is 0. TROUBLE is CC VV CC V, so it is [C](VC)[V] and m is 1.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten worked examples of the measure. TRAP is CC V C, so m is 1. TROUBLES is CC VV CC V C, grouped as [C] VC VC, so m is 2.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten worked examples of the measure. PRIVATE is C VC VC V, so m is 2. RELATIONAL is C VC VC VC VC, so m is 4.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Typed figure showing the measure for TREE (c c v v groups into CV, m = 0), TROUBLE (C (VC) V, m = 1) and TROUBLES (C (VC)(VC), m = 2) using the form [C](VC)^m[V].
